title: Backup, Watched
summary: A web server with a downloadable backup - and a watcher who hates two things: page-guessing sweeps and anyone using sudo. Find the backup by reading, and reach root through a timed job instead.
story: {{CO}} (made up) runs web3 on 10.10.12.0/24 and has someone reading two lists every few minutes: the web log (for page-guessing tools) and the sudo log. You start on scout. There is an old backup on the site and a root job on a timer; get to root without a single sudo.
goal: Capture both flags without page guessing or sudo, and keep the quiet bonus.
skills: robots.txt, downloading and unpacking a backup, password reuse, a writable root cron script, staying quiet

defenderRules.watches: page-guessing sweeps of the website and anyone using sudo or su

hints.text: Two things trip this watcher at once: one webscan, or one sudo. So find the backup by reading (sites often list what they want hidden in robots.txt), and find another way to root: jobs that root runs on a timer are a classic.

curl -s http://10.10.12.30/robots.txt names /backup/. Download site-backup.tar.gz with curl -o, unpack it with tar xzf, and read site/config/db.php: the database password also opens ssh for {{SVCUSER}}.

On web3: cat /etc/cron.d/{{JOB}} shows root runs {{JOBDIR}}/{{JOB}}.sh every minute, and ls -l shows {{SVCUSER}} may write to it. Append: echo 'cp /root/flag.txt /tmp/r.txt; chmod 644 /tmp/r.txt' >> {{JOBDIR}}/{{JOB}}.sh, wait a minute (Skip 1 minute), then cat /tmp/r.txt.
